evs-360.title: High-speed electric train EVS-360
evs-360.description: High-speed electric train platform for the first VSM line Moscow – Saint Petersburg: a joint engineering and production programme with phased delivery of trains for testing and certification.
facts: Joint work by ECRT and an industrial partner on design, manufacturing, and testing.
Calendar milestones and phase distribution are shown in the charts below; design documentation readiness metrics are updated in internal reporting.
A dedicated engineering workstream covers calculations of components, loads, and track–rolling stock interaction.
details: The EVS 360 project covers not only train development but also analytical verification of infrastructure interface elements: clamps, fastening nodes, track superstructure, and train–track interaction scenarios.
Analytical models help assess rolling stock loads on components, track dynamics, design stiffness of fastenings, component durability, and node behaviour within the track superstructure in advance.

The public page presents materials designed to remain stable across updates: cycle priorities, a development chart for subsystems, an integrated programme schedule, and examples of calculation workstreams. Detailed metrics are not published to avoid becoming outdated between releases.

ks-400-model.title: Catenary mathematical model
ks-400-model.status: Testing and validation of the mathematical model
ks-400-model.teaser: The catenary mathematical model enables finite-element calculations of static catenary performance and of dynamic interaction between the catenary and electric rolling stock pantographs.
ks-400-model.description: The model is intended for use in developing technical solutions, designing, and operating the catenary on all electrified sections of the Russian Railways network (including the Moscow – Saint Petersburg high-speed line) and for determining (and refining) the most rational parameters of catenary nodes and structures (such as catenary suspension, anchor-span junctions, average anchoring, air turnouts, supporting and bracing structures, fittings, and so on) while meeting current collection quality requirements at design speeds.
bullets: Catenary model: beam-based, with distributed parameters, built on the finite element method with modelling of catenary suspension, supports, bracing, and other structures, as well as conductors of various purpose in a single static and dynamic system.
Pantograph models: two-, three-, and four-mass with lumped parameters and rigid bodies, based on multibody dynamics, including combined configurations.
Interaction model: based on solving the contact problem using the penalty method.

sections.title: Verification against EN 50318:2018+A1:2022
paragraphs: Verification on reference models according to EN 50318:2018 was carried out for two model variants: non-sprung and sprung AC catenary suspension. Dynamic pantograph interaction modelling was performed at speeds of 275 and 320 km/h.

Verification by comparison with field test results cited in EN 50318:2018 was performed for two variants: non-sprung and sprung AC catenary suspension. The catenary suspension models comprised three anchor spans, and the analysis sections were over one kilometre long with 22 spans per model.

sections.title: Validation of the static KS-400 catenary mathematical model at the VNIIZHT experimental ring
paragraphs: Validation of the static KS-400 catenary mathematical model based on operational trials of the KS-400 catenary product range at the VNIIZHT experimental ring was performed by comparing calculated catenary suspension elasticity with field test data. Elasticity values were compared under each dropper and in inter-dropper spans of the analysed suspension sections. The maximum elasticity difference at all control points was 9.5%; the mean deviation was 3%.

ks-400-catenary.title: KS-400 product range
ks-400-catenary.teaser: R&D on the KS-400 catenary product range for VSM: structures, testing, and a pilot site at the VNIIZHT experimental ring under emergency operating modes.
ks-400-catenary.description:
The product range is designed for building the KS-400 railway catenary, providing reliable transfer of electrical energy from traction substations and line-side power supply equipment to electric rolling stock pantographs at train speeds up to 400 km/h.

Prototype trials on the VNIIZHT experimental ring were completed in 2026; design documentation has been assigned release «O1». ECRT and Russian Railways are now working together to put KS-400 catenary components into production.
bullets: Under the R&D programme, ECRT has developed structural elements, anchorage nodes, supporting and fixing structures, fittings and droppers, insulators, and structures for earthing and the return traction network of KS-400.
Prototype samples have been manufactured; preliminary, operational, and acceptance tests have been conducted with iterative improvement of design documentation and successful acceptance commissions.

sections.title: R&D scope and testing
paragraphs: Development of the KS-400 catenary product range is carried out for the first VSM line Moscow – Saint Petersburg.

Under the R&D programme, ECRT specialists developed structural elements, anchorage nodes, supporting and fixing structures, fittings and droppers, insulators, and structures for earthing and the return traction network of the KS-400 catenary. Prototype samples were manufactured; preliminary, operational, and acceptance tests of product range elements were conducted.
Design documentation was continuously refined throughout the work, enabling successful acceptance commissions.

sections.title: KS-400 catenary pilot site at the VNIIZHT experimental ring
paragraphs: Particular attention was given to the KS-400 catenary pilot site at the VNIIZHT experimental ring.

ECRT specialists, including using the developed mathematical model, together with the Russian Railways construction division, obtained unique results in high-precision catenary suspension adjustment and precise construction and installation work, achieving design positions within tight tolerances.

sections.title: Operational testing and emergency modes
paragraphs: At the VNIIZHT experimental ring, operational tests included experiments analysing KS-400 catenary suspension behaviour under emergency operating modes.

calculations.heading: Mathematical modelling and design calculations
calculations.intro: For the EVS 360 programme, the calculation framework links the train, track, and fastening elements — from clamp geometry to node behaviour within the track superstructure.

directions.title: Clamp calculations
directions.body: Optimisation of clamp geometry considering durability, natural frequency, and clamping force. Design stiffness of the fastening node is assessed separately.

directions.title: Track–rolling stock interaction
directions.body: Calculation of rolling stock loads on the node, accounting for track dynamics and various train–infrastructure interaction scenarios.

directions.title: Node calculations
directions.body: Verification of the fastening node for strength and durability using a computational mesh and an engineering contact model of the components.

directions.title: Node within the track structure
directions.body: Calculation of the node within the track superstructure, assessing rail stiffness and the elastic modulus of the sub-rail foundation.

sections.title: About the project
paragraphs: ECRT, commissioned by Russian Railways, is developing low-floor rolling stock for operation on low-traffic lines of Russian Railways. The approved working designation of the model range under development is:
A technical specification for RA12 has been developed; detailed design is in progress.
Forecast serial production volumes for rail buses are 300 cars (75 cars per year over 4 years) for operation on low-traffic lines of the Russian Railways network.

Creating modern rolling stock for passenger services on low-traffic sections of the Russian Railways network addresses the acute social challenge of transport accessibility to remote settlements for residents across the country.
bullets: rail bus RA11 — single-car version
rail bus RA12 — two-car version
rail bus RA13 — two-car version with enhanced-comfort car interiors

sections.title: Rolling stock configurations
paragraphs: Based on analysis of route network data and passenger traffic volumes on low-traffic railway lines, development and deployment of two rolling stock types is planned:
bullets: For routes up to 50 km in length, a single-car multiple unit with a power plant based on a rechargeable energy storage system and an auxiliary diesel-generator unit, 58 seats and a design capacity (seated plus 3 persons/m² standing on free floor area) of 93 passengers in a 3rd-class interior layout (3+2 seating)
For routes over 50 km in length, a two-car multiple unit with a booster section containing two diesel-generator units, 126 seats and a design capacity of 192 passengers in a 3rd-class interior layout

metrics.label: Single-car multiple unit: seats and design capacity, passengers
Two-section multiple unit: seats and design capacity, passengers

sections.title: Platform requirements
paragraphs: A key parameter for both rolling stock types is a reduced floor height providing barrier-free access (without steps or stairs) for passengers boarding and alighting on railway lines equipped with low passenger platforms at a nominal height of 200 mm. Boarding from ground level is also envisaged.

metrics.label: Nominal height of low passenger platforms

sections.title: Programme context
paragraphs: Russian Railways has initiated a project to create low-floor rolling stock for operation on low-traffic sections of the Russian Railways network.

New rolling stock is being created to replace the retiring rail bus fleet: the existing DT1, RA1, and RA2 diesel train fleet will be withdrawn from service between 2030 and 2040 upon reaching end of service life, while production of the RA3 modification developed as a replacement was halted by Transmashholding (TMH) in 2022 due to unavailability of key components (underfloor power plant). Resumption of production of this rolling stock is not planned in the medium term. TMH is currently developing a low-floor rolling stock platform of three or more cars, whose operation on low-traffic lines is inefficient.
In view of this, Russian Railways has decided to develop rolling stock in single-car and two-car configurations in-house, meeting the requirements for operation on low-traffic lines.

The Russian Railways network currently totals 85.6 thousand kilometres. Of these, 360 lines totalling 15.47 thousand km are low-traffic sections. Nearly half of all low-traffic lines have social and defence significance. Marketing research also indicates a need to organise services on new routes on low-traffic lines, requiring new rolling stock. A fundamentally new rolling stock type is therefore required for efficient operation on low-traffic sections.

metrics.label: Withdrawal period for the DT1, RA1, and RA2 fleet

sections.title: About the project
paragraphs: JSC Engineering Centre of Railway Transport (ECRT) has established a dedicated unit for developing advanced track infrastructure solutions (Infrastructure Development Centre).

Under the Russian Railways programme to create a track structure and maintenance technologies providing 2.5 billion gross tonnes of throughput, the Centre acts as developer of the structure, its elements, and maintenance technologies, and as coordinator of all project participants.
The project goal is to reduce track life-cycle cost on heavily loaded sections by extending gross tonnage throughput between capital and intermediate track maintenance cycles.
R&D and deployment of maintenance technologies for the innovative track structure are carried out from 2021 to 2026.

sections.title: Main workstreams
bullets: Development of track structure elements with improved operational and resource characteristics
Addressing the integrated challenge of synergising technical characteristics of track elements within a unified structure
Creating a maintenance and monitoring system enabling effective reliability of the track structure
Creating a complex of mathematical models for the railway track

sections.title: Competence ecosystem
paragraphs: The project is complex and research-intensive, leading Russian competence centres have been engaged across the following areas:
bullets: infrastructure design bureau (PCB I);
specialist research organisations and higher education institutions: VNIIZHT, RUT (MIIT), PGUPS, SGUPS, ICT VEIP, and Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University;
manufacturers and developers of track superstructure elements and structures: EVRAZ, Novosibirsk and Murom switch plants, RZDstroy, BetElTrans (BET), and others.

sections.title: Maintenance schemes
paragraphs: Preliminary maintenance schemes are defined by the Technical Requirements for track structure and maintenance system.
Key target indicators:

metrics.label: Target gross throughput between capital track maintenance cycles
Increase in gross throughput between intermediate maintenance cycles
Increase in gross throughput between intermediate maintenance cycles for sections with complex alignment and profile

paragraphsAfterMetrics: Accordingly, an important aspect of project implementation is ensuring compliance with criteria for both the first limit state (strength and stability) and the second limit state (stability of track position in plan and profile).

sections.title: Rollout outlook
paragraphs: Installation (rollout) of new track structures, identified as most effective according to the technical and economic justification, is planned to begin on heavily loaded sections of the Russian Railways network from 2027.
All heavily loaded sections of the Russian Railways network — more than 17 thousand km — are prospective rollout sites for the developed innovative track structure.

fieldWorks.heading: Technology deployment
fieldWorks.intro: Three sequential stages: track panel assembly at a track maintenance depot, subgrade preparation using cold recycling technology, and panel installation on a section of the Krasnoyarsk Railway.

stages.title: Track panel assembly at the track maintenance depot
stages.description: Assembly of the track panel with intermediate rail fastenings and sleepers developed under the project at a track maintenance depot (TMD).

stages.title: Subgrade preparation and sub-ballast protective layer installation
stages.description: Removal of the existing track panel followed by installation of a sub-ballast protective layer using cold recycling technology. The protective layer installation process was developed by ECRT.

stages.title: Track panel installation on the Russian Railways network
stages.description: Installation of the innovative track structure on a section of the Krasnoyarsk Railway.

modeling.heading: Mathematical modelling and track structure calculations
modeling.intro: Mathematical modelling receives substantial attention during project implementation. A suite of mathematical models has been developed and is used for design and calculations of innovative track structures. All models have been validated based on experiments conducted by VNIIZHT, MIIT, and ICT VEIP.

testingNote.title: Testing and validation of characteristics
testingNote.body: During project implementation, a comprehensive programme of preliminary (factory), laboratory, and bench testing was completed, confirming the characteristics of the innovative track structure under development and its elements.

blocks.title: Analysis of dynamic track–rolling stock interaction
blocks.body: Multi-body dynamic modelling accounts for all aspects of rolling stock suspension and track superstructure design to determine loads from the wheel on the rails.

blocks.title: Calculation of stress–strain state of track superstructure
blocks.body: Dynamic loads obtained are applied to a finite-element model of the track superstructure to determine rail deflection and uplift, instantaneous sleeper settlements, and vertical and lateral loads on rail fastening nodes. Rail strength and track stability are determined.

blocks.title: Strength calculation of intermediate rail fastenings and concrete sleepers
blocks.body: Detailed finite-element models of fastenings determine their translational and rotational stiffness, assess strength and deformability of structural elements, and determine elastic clamp service life. Detailed sleeper models account for prestressing of reinforcing elements and allow crack development in concrete to be determined.

blocks.title: Geotechnical modelling of the sub-sleeper foundation
blocks.body: Specialised geotechnical finite-element models are used to determine deformability and stability of the ballast prism, embankment, and foundation, including possible strengthening of the main embankment platform.

blocks.title: Optimisation of track superstructure elements
blocks.body: Multi-criteria parametric optimisation is used to obtain three-dimensional geometry of elastic clamps with high clamping force, fatigue durability, and natural vibration frequencies. Reinforcement of concrete sleepers and required deformability indicators of track structure materials are also optimised.

operationalTesting.heading: Operational testing
paragraphs: To conduct operational testing of the innovative track structure, in autumn 2023 at the Experimental Ring at Shcherbinka station, test and control track sections were installed in curves with radii of 1200, 590, and 400 m. Thirteen test sections with a total length of 650 metres were laid with various rail-and-sleeper grid configurations, along with five control sections with a total length of 295 metres.
On the test sections, a ballast layer of basalt rock in a new fraction from 10 to 63 mm was installed. An experimental cold recycling process for the sub-ballast protective layer was also developed.

In autumn 2024, at the Experimental Ring at Shcherbinka station, innovative 1/11 turnouts with a continuous running surface — with and without cant on the rail strings — a 1/13 diverging turnout with a continuous running surface and cant on the rail strings, and a high-durability insulated joint were installed for operational testing.
Operational testing of the innovative track structure was completed in autumn 2025.
